org.name: Tameside and Glossop Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust

hazard: Fragmented and disjointed information storage and sharing

reports.title: Lila Marsland: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: Having carefully considered the oral evidence given in court by a range of different clinicians with varying roles and remits, I am concerned that, notwithstanding the work the Trust has undertaken in response to Lila's death, the Child Sepsis Screening Tool is not yet fully embedded in the minds of those who assess and treat Children and Young People at the Trust
concerns.hazard: lack of full embedding of Child Sepsis Screening Tool

concerns.quote: I am concerned that the Trust is yet to fully implement the latest iteration of the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence's Guideline Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management (NG240 Published 19 March 2024)
concerns.hazard: lack of full implementation of NG240 guideline

concerns.quote: It is a matter of concern that the Locum Consultant in Emergency Medicine who completed a form indicating Lila was 'Safe to Transfer' to the Paediatric Emergency Department did so without undertaking any examination or direct assessment of her
concerns.hazard: locum consultant signed 'Safe to Transfer' without examination

concerns.quote: I am concerned that no medical record appears to exist of the examination of Lila which was undertaken by the Locum Registrar in Paediatrics which resulted was discharged from hospital
concerns.hazard: absence of medical record of examination by Locum Registrar in Paediatrics

concerns.quote: the Child Sepsis Screening Tool is not yet fully embedded in the minds of those who assess and treat Children and Young People at the Trust
concerns.hazard: lack of full embedding of Child Sepsis Screening Tool

concerns.quote: over the course of almost 10 hours in hospital, Lila's history and details of examinations and assessments undertaken were recorded on a mixture of various analogue and digital systems in operation in different parts of the Trust, leading to a risk of vital clinical information being lost in the system
concerns.hazard: fragmented and disjointed information storage and sharing

reports.title: Margaret Murphy: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: A consultant in medical microbiology gave evidence as to a national shortage of doctors of that specialism in the NHS. Given the significance of microbiology to modern medicine, I am concerned any such shortage creates a risk of future deaths
concerns.hazard: national shortage of medical microbiology doctors

concerns.quote: The court heard evidence that Tameside Hospital relies on an off-site laboratory to undertake and report on microbiology tests such as blood-cultures. Whilst not a relevant factor in Miss [name redacted] case, I am concerned as to the impact this system has for the time it takes relevant results to reach treating clinicians
concerns.hazard: off-site laboratory processing of microbiology tests

concerns.quote: Having reviewed Miss Murphy in the Same Day Emergency Care Unit on 5 October 2025, the Orthopaedic Senior House Officer wrote their notes in a Trauma and Orthopaedic 'Tracker', not routinely accessible to clinicians working in other specialities. I am concerned as to the risk of future deaths which arises from the creation of an extra layer of documentation not easily visible to others in the hospital, particularly in the context of an already disjointed and labyrinthine system for capturing clinical information

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that clinical information is recorded in ways that are not readily accessible across the Trust, creating a risk of vital data being lost or overlooked.
